extracted.intended_audience: content marketers, digital publishers, journalists, and editors interested in explainer-format content
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating 'explainer' journalism/content — SEO-friendly, question-centered explanatory pieces used by digital publishers and brands. Focuses on structure, staffing, editorial judgment, and reuse across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainer answers and anticipates reader questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital media doesn’t just tell stories anymore; it answers questions and anticipates follow-up inquiries, delivering explanatory content on intricacies you might have missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vox-style explainers are 'spoon-fed' around questions readers have; best explainers 'beat a reader to a question' and answer queries readers may not have thought to ask. Examples: Vox headlines like '...explained' and '9 questions you were too embarrassed to ask.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Adds context to a simple question
rubrics_metrics.description: "A great explainer adds context to a simple question." (Ezra Klein)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explainers should go beyond a basic definition or terse summary; they should situate a simple query within broader background, mechanics, or implications so readers understand why the answer matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must add something beyond aggregated information
rubrics_metrics.description: Nix any story that doesn't add anything to a simple query; avoid publishing content that's merely 'Popular Google search term + aggregated information from other sources = viral content.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation alone is insufficient: publishers should provide original synthesis, analysis, reporting, or perspective rather than churned, formulaic collections of other outlets' material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use search data for inspiration but exercise editorial judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox's team used (and still uses) search engine data as a loose inspiration for their editorial calendar: 'Search is a very easy thing to be inspired by... it's whatever people are asking about today in the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage search trends to find audience questions, but only pursue topics where the publisher can add substantive value beyond what currently exists online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure explainers around sub-questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Break an explainer into sub-questions the audience is likely to ask (e.g., Vox's impeachment piece 'broken into sub-questions that Vox assumes might arise').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content as a series of anticipated FAQs or thematic subheads so readers can quickly find the specific facet they care about and the piece can be updated iteratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire obsessives/subject-matter experts, not only journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox's hiring mantra: 'Obsessives first.' They hired many people who were not journalists but were top professionals in their fields and deeply passionate about the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer contributors with deep curiosity and domain expertise; reporters can be taught reporting skills, but obsession and subject knowledge produce better explainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent, archivable, linkable, embeddable content; length isn't a problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Explainers should be 'archivable... linkable... embeddable, persistent, and length isn't a problem.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design explainers as evergreen assets that can be updated and referenced over time; longer form and iterative updates are acceptable and often beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect reader intelligence; avoid being patronizing or oversimplifying
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics argue explanatory journalism can be patronizing—reducing complex stories to three-paragraph definitions—whereas Klein believed audiences were 'smarter than that.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dumbing-down content; provide nuance and depth so readers who seek deeper answers find them rather than simple 'news for kids' summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid formulaic explainers that stifle creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that follows the simple search+aggregation equation 'quickly stifles both creators and their audience' and makes media homogenous and boring when saturated with lazy explainers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage editorial risk, unique angles, and creative formats to prevent commodification of the explainer form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate, entertain, and own your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal is the same, whether you’re a brand selling a product or a digital media company: You have to educate, entertain, and own your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance informative depth with engaging storytelling and build a recognizable editorial voice that fosters repeat engagement and audience loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthy content that contextualizes claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Like Vox, brands such as Mint 'strive to create trustworthy content and contextualize relevant news stories for their audience.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence, explain trade-offs, and situate claims in context (e.g., financial explainers should clearly explain risks and mechanics) to build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer questions readers hadn't thought to ask (novel angles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the best explainers 'answer questions that haven't occurred to readers yet'—the ones that make you say, 'Oh, I’ve never really thought about that before.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek surprising or curiosity-driven topics and frames that reveal overlooked aspects of familiar subjects to increase engagement and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repurpose explainers across platforms and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: After Vox set up this content model, it was easy to expand into an explainer podcast, a Netflix series, a YouTube channel, Snapchat Discover, and brand-sponsored projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create explainers with modular components that can be adapted into video, audio, infographics, and sponsored content while preserving core explanatory value.

rubrics_metrics.name: For branded explainers: maintain an educational stance and manage conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The educational aspect helps brands avoid reporting on conflicts of interest or criticizing their own industries; branded explainers 'position the writer as an authority figure' or SME.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When brands produce explainers, prioritize transparency and contextualization so content educates rather than functions solely as promotional material; explicitly disclose sponsorship and avoid misleading authority claims.
